key_insight: A physics-informed neural network can learn interpretable corrections to a simple k-ε-b turbulence closure, improving Rayleigh-Taylor mixing predictions during the transition to turbulence.
engineering_relevance: This offers a path to more reliable, calibrated RANS closures for unsteady buoyancy-driven flows where standard turbulence models struggle before fully developed turbulence.
method: Embed the k-ε-b model inside a surrogate PINN.
Learn both coefficient calibrations and missing corrective terms from DNS data.
Re-express the learned corrections as explicit analytical modifications of the closure.
evidence_signal: The corrected model is evaluated against an extensive DNS database of Rayleigh-Taylor flows and shows improved predictions of mixing-layer growth during transition.
watch_item: The approach is trained and validated on Rayleigh-Taylor DNS, so transferability to other flow regimes or stronger extrapolation remains uncertain.
paper_title: Learning Turbulence Closures with Physics-Informed Neural Networks for the Rayleigh-Taylor Transition to Turbulence
